SUBJECT:  PROPOSED  MURAL  FOR  3420 FIRESTONE  BOULEV  ARD  - KFC

PURPOSE:  To review  a request  to paint  an outdoor  mural  at 3420 Firestone  Boulevard.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:

  a.  CONSIDER  the proposed  painted  mural  for 3420 Firestone  Boulevard,  KFC.

ANALYSIS:  On March  1, 2022,  the Planning  Commission  approved  Conditional  Use Permit  No.  852 to allow
the construction  and operation  of a new 1,797  square-foot  fast food restaurant  with  a drive-through,  in the Civic
Center zone, at 3420 Firestone  Boulevard.  Pursuant  to South Gate Municipal  Code Chapter  11.36 "Signs,"  murals
which  do "not  pertain  to the business,  product  or service  rendered  on the premises  shall be considered  a mural,"
and requires  the review  of the Plaru'iing  Commission.

The proposed  mural  would  be painted  along  the existing  8-foot  block  wall  located  along  the southern  property
line of the subject  property.  The mural  would  be visible  to visitors  and patrons  inside  both the parking  lot and the
drive-through  lane of the restaurant.  The proposed  mural  will  measure  approximately  30 feet in width  and 8 feet
in height.  Because  this  project  will  be installed  on private  property,  maintenance  of the mural  will  be the
responsibility  of the business  owner.  The proposed  artwork  is an image  of three children  painting  a chicken,  eating
corn  and  drinking  a soda,  portrayed  with  bright  and  lively  colors  (Attachment  A).  The  mural's  artist,
"Bumblebeelovesyou,"  describes  the proposed  mural  with  the following:

  "Whimsical, playful with a sense of childish innocence, freedom and joy. In all my
  work I try to keep the childhood spirit alive. People grow up too fast. In my work I
  want to help people remember, even ifjust for a secorid, what it was like when to
  be a kid again.  I work  with  schools,  private  organizations,  and business  oviners  to
  create one of a kind site-specific murals that are bespoke to their business or
  organization. My goal as an artist is to create images that are representative of the
  business or school they are on while keeping with my overall artist theme of
  playfulness and whimsy."

The Planning  Commission  is charged  with  reviewing  mural  requests  including  size, height  and location.

Conditions
The conditions  found  in Attachment  A are imposed  on the subject  mural  project.

SUBJECT:  A COMPLIANCE  REVIEW  OF PREVIOUSLY  APPROVED  CONDITIONAL
USE  PERMITS  FOR  ALCOHOL  SALES

PURPOSE:  A compliance  review  of previously  reviewed  and approved  conditional  use permits
for alcohol  sales throughout  the City.

BACKGROUND:  Pursuant  to South  Gate Municipal  Code Chapter  11.42 "Alcoholic  Beverage
Sales,"  "permits  are subject  to compliance  review  of the property  and Conditional  Use Permit
(CUP)  conditions  at planning-commission-established  intervals;  the first  compliance  review  shall
occur within  six months  of permit  issuance  or actuation."

The following  are the recent  CUP approvals  for alcohol  sales that were approved  by the Planning
Commission.  Applicants  then proceeded  to obtain  alcohol  licenses  from the California  Department
of Alcoholic  Beverage  Control  (ABC).

1. CUP No. 846 for Northgate Market at 4155 TweedyBlvd, approved July 6, 2021
  Applicant  added  an ABC  Type  86 License  (Instructional  tasting)  to an existing  ABC  Type  21
  License  (Off-sale  general)  at an existing  market.

2. CUP No. 851 for Red Tacos at 9322 Long Beach Blvd., approved September 7, 2021
  Applicant  requested  the approval  of an ABC  Type  41 License  (On-sale  beer and wine),  in
  conjunction  with  a restaurant.

3. CUP No. 856 for a brewery at 3606 Tweedy Blvd., approved Febrriary 15, 2022
  Applicant  requested  the approval  of an ABC  Type  2 License  (Winegrower)  and Type  23
  License  (Small  beer manufacturer),  in conjunction  with  a restaurant.

Planning  staff  requested  pertinent  information  regarding  the subject  licenses  listed  above  and
attached  of  the  Police  Department  and  the  Code  Enforcement  Division  of  the  Community
Development  Department.  Both  departments  noted  that the sales of alcohol  have not caused  for
property  nuisances,  maintenance  or disturbance  calls. Therefore,  Planning  staff did not contact  the
above-mentioned  businesses  regarding  the review  of their conditional  use permit  approvals  and/or
ABC  licenses.

  1.  The  property  is located  within  the former  Lucky's  and Save-On  Pharmacy,  at a

  5.  Instructional  tasting will  operate Monday  thru Sunday from 10:00 A.M.  to 9:00 P.M.

  WHEREAS,  the City Planning  Commission  made the following  findings:

  1.  Approval  of the CUP is consistent  with,  and will  not adversely  affect,  the intent  and

  The proposed  project  is located with the TMU2  of the Tweedy  Boulevard  Specific  Plan

  single use retail such as large format  supermarkets.  The instructional  tasting  of alcohol

  2.  The design and development  of the land use and conditions  of the CUP are compatible
  with the existing  and future  land uses of the applicable  zone.

  3.  Approval  of the CUP  would  not result  in detrimental  impacts  to adjacent  properties  or
  to the character  or function  of the neighborhood.

  Facilities)Sectionl5301oftheCaliforniaEnvironmentalQualityAct.  Classlconsists

  of  existing  public  or  private  structures,  facilities,  mechanical  equipment,  or
  topographical  features,  involving  negligible  or no expansion  ofuse  beyond  that existing
  at the time  of the lead agency's  determination.  The project  is exempt  under  Class  1

  structure.

  NOW,  THEREFORE,  BE  IT  RESOLVED,  that the Planning  Commission  of the City  of
South  Gate,  pursuant  to the facts,  noted  above,  does hereby  approve  Conditional  Use Permit  No.
846 to allow  Type  86 (instructional  tasting  license)  to an existing  Type  21 license  at the Northgate
Market,  subject  to the conditions  of approval  contained  in Exhibit  A.

This  recommendation  was adopted  by the following  vote at the Planning  Commission  meeting  of

 31. Violation  Signage
  For the duration  of any suspension  of an alcohol-related  CUP,  the Planning  Commission,
  or, upon  any  appeal,  the City  Council,  may  direct  the permittee  to post  a sign  on the
  premises  of the establishment  relating  to such suspension.  The size, content,  and location
  of such sign shall  be as specified  by the Director.

32. Violation  of Conditional  Use Permit
  A public  hearing  consistent  with  Chapter  11.50  (Administration)  shall  be held  for  the
  consideration  of a permit  revocation.  A permit  or any associated  conditions  may be revoked
  or modified  by the Planning  Commission  subject  to any of the following  grounds:

  a.  The permit  or approval  was obtained  by fraud.

  b.  The property  is not being  use for the purpose  which  is the subject  of the permit.
  c.  The use for which  the approval  was granted  has ceased or has been suspended  for
  I year or more.

  d.  The permit  or conditions  of the approval  have been violated;  exercised  contrary  to
  the terms  of approval;  or in violation  of any statute,  ordinance,  law or regulation.

  e.  The use for which  the approval  was granted  was exercised  in a manner  detrimental
  to the public  health  or safety,  or as to constitute  a public  nuisance.

33. Conditional  Use Permit  Expiration
  Any  approval  or permit  granted  by the City  becomes  null  and void  if the property  is not
  being  used  for  the  approved  or permitted  purpose  within  one  year  from  the  date  the
  approval  or permits  was issued,  consistent  with  the provisions  identified  within  Section
  11.55 Nonconforming  Uses and Buildings.

34. Conditional  Use Permit  Revocation
  If the application  or any conditions  of the CUP  violate  the Zoning  Code  or do not fulfill
  the intent  of the Code,  the Planning  Commission  shall,  following  a public  hearing,  be
  authorized  to take the following  actions:

  a.  Revoke  the CUP,  revoke  and reissue  the CUP with  new or modified  conditions,  or
  modify  the  conditions  of  the  existing  CUP  as may  be appropriate  under  the
  circumstances.
  b.  Impose,  as a condition  of the continuation,  reinstatement,  or reissuance  of the CUP,
  a requirement  that  the permittee  reimburse  the  City  for  all  costs  and  expenses
  reasonably  incurred  in investigating,  identifying,  and documenting  the violation,
  and  in processing  information  concerning  the  violation  for  presentation  to the
  Planning  Commission,  and, upon any appeal,  to the City  Council.
